items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: So I started to taking lessons from Preston. And that's when I really learned what the trombone was about, you know.

ctx.x: Well, some people were in fact, maybe others not. Can you tell me anything else about any other teachers you had or other trombone players you listened to? And maybe if you didn't study with them that you learned from them by...

Well, who has done more for me than anyone? Well, as I said, I was with Jackson for a few years, and he gave me all the fundamentals of things. But Preston Jackson was with the band. There was a place at 43rd and State Street upstairs. It was called the Red Mill. And, of course, I was on...it was just a dance hall. And it ran every Sunday. Every Sunday evening they would have matinee dances. And, of course, you couldn't get in there unless you had on long pants. Well, in those days, I mean, the boys, if you were…
Is he still around? No, he passed.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Well Al Wynn was with him then.

ctx.x: It's nice paying everything. You want to stick me?

Yeah, well we had him play Stickney. He was out there steady. I forget to call it the Red something. Red Arrow. Yeah Red Arrow. Well Al Wynn was with him then. I played out there with Lil Armstrong a couple of times, but he had Al Wynn with him then. I played with him showboat later. When I joined him, I joined him and went in the showboat. Then we went out east and New England did some concerts and things like that. But we're doing pretty nice. Most of August, we work most of August. It's nice pay. I work a…
Barbara Reed used to help promote those dances. Do you remember Barbara and Bill Reed? They used to help promote dances at the Midnight Sun in Chicago.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And at one time there was Blake, Al Wynn, myself, and this boy would die.

ctx.x: Well I wanted to play the clarinet.

Did you ever get the clarinet at all? That's why it'd take me so long with the trombone, see. No, never did, nothing but the trombone. After I began to play it and people would take notes and I'd say well I'd just go ahead on through with it. I'm glad I did now. Because they told me, he says, there isn't but a few, at that time you didn't have the musicians they have now, everywhere you look, he says there ain't but a few good trombone players around here. And I held the top up top there around here, not…
I talked to him the other day.
